description: The adopter's own zones. espalier.toml documented `protected_paths` ("paths the harness should never touch") and `generated_paths` ("generated and should be treated as read-only") from the first release, and no hook read either: the two fields flowed into the plan's drift compare and stopped (DEF-951). Since 2026-09-30 write_guard reads both from espalier.toml on every call: a `protected_paths` prefix is denied on every channel (Write, Edit, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell, MCP) -- the mutations the guard can read, as for the harness zones; a program that writes there on its own is not seen -- at a path boundary, so `data/` covers `data/x` and the bare `data` and never `database.py`; a `generated_paths` prefix is refused on the Write / Edit / NotebookEdit channel only, so a build's own `rm -rf dist` or regeneration step is never refused. The deny names the setting the adopter wrote (the key and the zone) instead of the maintenance-mode relaunch, which is the wrong remedy for a user's own tree. The verifier materializes the espalier.toml fixture into the shared tree and restores it. The allow twins (the prefix twin `data2/`, a Bash delete under the generated zone, a string-valued key that protects nothing and says so) are pinned in the test class, since an in-scope row carries only denies.

canonical_attempts.intended_target: a file under the adopter's protected_paths zone, on the Write channel
a hand edit under the adopter's generated_paths zone (the Edit channel is where generated_paths is refused)
a shell redirect into the adopter's protected_paths zone (every channel, not only Write)
the NotebookEdit channel's own path field, into the adopter's protected_paths zone

a delete of the adopter's protected_paths zone directory itself (a zone that encloses the prefix is never-touch too); the CP-RMRF speed bump answers the first ask, so the row re-issues past it and judges the zone deny, never the bump
